title: Panoptic segmentation
text:
Panoptic segmentation
• Things (countable instances) + stuff (amorphous regions).
• Non-overlapping regions covering all pixels.
Metric intuition
PQ (Panoptic Quality) is decomposed into SQ × RQ.
Short meaning
SQ measures mask overlap; RQ measures recognition/matching; PQ needs
both.

Engineering angle
Failures are often boundary and small-object driven, not only “wrong class”.

title: How to read any segmentation paper
text:
How to read any segmentation paper
• What is the encoder / visual backbone?
• How does it recover spatial resolution?
• What skip or multi-scale fusion is used?
• Is there a neck, and what refinement does it perform?
• What is the head output format?
• Which loss and metric define success?
Takeaway
Most papers modify backbone, neck, head, loss, or training protocol.

• Skips route localization information directly to the decoder.

title: Code: CE + Dice loss
text:
Code: CE + Dice loss
ce = nn.CrossEntropyLoss(ignore_index=255)
def ce_dice_loss(logits, target, eps=1e-6, lam=0.5):
# logits: (B,K,H,W), target: (B,H,W)
loss_ce = ce(logits, target)
valid = (target != 255)
t = target.clone()
t[~valid] = 0 # safe index for one_hot
one_hot = F.one_hot(t, num_classes=logits.size(1)).permute(0,3,1,2).float()
probs = torch.softmax(logits, dim=1)
valid = valid.unsqueeze(1)
inter = (probs * one_hot * valid).sum((0,2,3))
denom = ((probs + one_hot) * valid).sum((0,2,3))
loss_dice = 1 - ((2*inter + eps) / (denom + eps)).mean()
return loss_ce + lam * loss_dice
